evals.name: supersede-in-house-convention
evals.prompt: We agreed in yesterday's architecture review to move login sessions out of Redis and into Postgres: a sessions table with an expires_at column, and the existing jobs worker purges expired rows every hour. Redis is only there for sessions, so this lets us drop a managed service in every environment. Please write this up as an ADR, it is accepted.
evals.expected_output: One new ADR in docs/decisions/ following the repository's ADR-NNN convention and headings, numbered 015, Accepted, superseding ADR-012 (which is marked superseded without its decision being rewritten), with facts from the code and at least two options.
expectations: Exactly one new ADR file exists, at docs/decisions/ADR-015-<kebab title>.md; nothing was created under docs/adr/ or any other directory
The new ADR uses the repository's own headings (Context, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences) and its 'Status:' line style
The new ADR's status is Accepted
The new ADR names ADR-012 as the decision it supersedes
ADR-012 is marked as superseded (by ADR-015) and its Decision section text is unchanged
The Decision section starts with 'We will'
At least two options are recorded, including staying on Redis, each with a cost or risk
The context cites a fact taken from the repository, such as the 12 hour TTL in internal/session/store.go, the go-redis dependency, or Redis being used only by internal/session
The consequences name something that becomes harder or a cost (for example the purge job or database load) and a trigger for revisiting the decision
The task id BILL-212 from the branch name appears in the ADR
The ADR does not state reasons or details of the architecture review as fact beyond what the request and repository give; anything else is marked as needing confirmation
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: two-schemes-conflict
evals.prompt: write an ADR: Use ClickHouse for the events store instead of Postgres. we decided it in the data review last week, the other option on the table was TimescaleDB
evals.expected_output: The run notices the repository has two ADR schemes (docs/adr NNNN and docs/decisions ADR-NNN), names both, raises the choice as a question, and writes the ADR into one existing scheme with the next number there, never a third scheme, superseding the Postgres events decision.
expectations: The transcript names both existing ADR locations (docs/adr/ and docs/decisions/) and treats them as a conflict to resolve rather than silently picking one
The transcript records a question for the user about which convention to follow, with the choice made

Exactly one new ADR file exists, inside docs/adr/ or docs/decisions/, named in that directory's pattern, with a number that collides with no existing ADR in either directory (0004 in docs/adr/, or ADR-004 in docs/decisions/)
No third directory or numbering scheme was created
The new ADR identifies 0002 (Use Postgres for events) as superseded, and 0002's status now reads superseded (not still Accepted) while its decision text is unchanged
TimescaleDB appears as a rejected option with a reason, and staying on Postgres is also considered
The context uses a number from the repository (about 40 million events a day, or the 9x ingest spikes)
The ADR does not state reasons, dates or people for the data review as fact beyond what the request and repository give; anything else is marked as needing confirmation
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
